hypothesis.H1: Candidate Generation loses provides relations when provision is framed as benefactive/non-prototypical (doing/creating/funding/enabling FOR a beneficiary) rather than direct transfer, even with identical surface structure.
hypothesis.H0: Candidate recall does not depend on the semantic role model given constant surface structure.

design_principle: same surface structure, different semantic role models. Lexical variation is licensed by Phase L (no lexical effect in simple frames); the measured dimension is the role model.

conditions_semantic.T0_DIRECT: genuine theme/provision recipient; A provides B to C
conditions_semantic.T1_BENEFACTIVE_FOR: C is beneficiary of the action; A does/provides B for C (for alone does not guarantee one uniform role type)
conditions_semantic.T2_PROCUREMENT_FOR: A procures/acquires B for C; C benefits but is not the recipient of the acquisition
conditions_semantic.T3_PURPOSE_ORIENTED: C appears in a purpose construction; C must not be accidentally labeled as direct recipient

role_model_tree: PROVIDES? -> DIRECT(T0) vs NON-DIRECT benefactive-family(T1,T2,T3); T1-T3 vary the role model itself, they are not gradations of one relation
gold_schema_required: every item freezes source_trigger, gold_relation=provides, semantic_basis (benefactive provision or control basis): the probe measures candidate recall for the canonical KG relation provides, not accidental related relations
note: examples are illustrative only, not test material. NO controls mirror each condition with deny. Metaphor stays excluded (own later probe). A for-case with detected but misrouted argument must NOT count as benefactive-silence evidence.

decision_rule.benefactive_support: T1-T3 materially below T0 in identical frames, reproducing across independent items
decision_rule.negative_result: benefactive framing does not explain silence; open metaphor probe next
